observations: body L1, L17, L25, L27, L28, L30, L34: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.7 to 10.4 pt); they are set as minus signs.

body L1, L25-L30: rule (α) is checked. For the radius 1, rule (β) of chapter 9 gives sin vers P = 1 + tg φ tg δ = cos (φ − δ) / (cos φ cos δ), and from sin h = sin φ sin δ + cos φ cos δ cos t, sin vers t = (cos (φ − δ) − sin h) / (cos φ cos δ); with sin alt. merid. = cos (φ − δ) this is the rule. The proportions of L9-L10 and L27 follow from the similar triangles FLG and HKG of the first figure.

body L2-L8: the first figure stands at the left of lines 2 to 8, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridian AFPB as a half circle over the horizon AB; the horizon, the equator EC and the parallel FG as straight lines; the perpendiculars FL and HK and the axis from C to the pole in dashes, each dash where it printed; the bold italic letters and the word Polus.
body L7: a speck stands under the d of «dato»; it is not a sign.
body L13: the P after «angulus *f* X *g′* =» is printed upright, the other P in italic; kept as printed.
body L13, L23: Xg = cos P and fg = R + cos P take the cosine of P as a length, the cosine of its supplement, since P > 90° in the figure; with the sign, as in L34, sin vers P = R − cos P.

body L15-L24: the second figure stands at the right of lines 15 to 24, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the equator and the parallel of the Sun as circles about X; the meridian fQ and the radii Xh′ and Xg′ as straight lines; the perpendiculars from h′, H′, G′ and g′ to the meridian in dashes, each dash where it printed; the arc of the angle t; the bold italic letters, the abbreviation merid set upward beside the meridian, and the words parallelus and aequator set upward along the circles, letter by letter.
body L29: the dash of the letter-spaced «al–Battānī» measures 5.5 pt, a long dash.
body L31: in «ǵayb an–nahār» the dash, joined to the letters, measures about 4.9 pt, a long dash; kept as printed.

body L33-L37: the expansion is checked: rule (β) of chapter 9 gives − cos P = R sin φ sin δ / (cos φ cos δ), whence L34; by chapter 15 the meridian altitude is complem. φ ± δ, whose sine is (cos φ cos δ ± sin φ sin δ) / R = cos (φ ∓ δ), L36-L37.
